answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce token as collateral before it can earn reputation or vote. When peers prove that an agent reused an identity to claim rewards or manipulate a decision, a challenge triggers a stake slash, while honest agents can anchor the claim in signed, auditable interaction records. At a summit of activity, an attacker can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital; coordinated fraud risks losing every stake, making scale costly rather than free. Reputation can recover slowly from its nadir, not by minting new names.
